literal.prompt: Из какого города советское правительство перенесло столицу в Москву в 1918 году?

literalGroups.primaryGround: The official Presidential Library account states that the Soviet government moved the capital from Petrograd to Moscow: institutions were to leave Petrograd 11-12 March and the 16 March resolution expressly names Petrograd as the source and Moscow as destination (PRlib L52-L55). Thus Petrograd is the unique key for this exact 1918 event. Every answer remains a city-name choice. The own-option notes independently ground Novgorod (museum L217-L220), Kyiv (Ukraine law L230-L235), and Nizhny Novgorod (MCHS L205-L206); they do not alter which city the 1918 transfer left.
literalGroups.locator: President Library L52-L55; Novgorod Museum L217-L220; President of Ukraine portal L230-L235; MCHS L205-L206

literalGroups.literal: Советское правительство перенесло столицу из Петрограда в Москву: 12 марта 1918 года Москва вновь стала столицей Советского государства. 16 марта IV Всероссийский съезд Советов временно закрепил этот перенос.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The Presidential Library dates Moscow becoming capital of the Soviet state to 12 March 1918 (L54) and quotes the 16 March resolution temporarily moving the RSFSR capital from Petrograd to Moscow (L55). This directly supports both sentences.

literalGroups.literal: Правительственные учреждения должны были переехать из Петрограда в Москву 11–12 марта 1918 года.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The Presidential Library states that all government institutions were to move from Petrograd to Moscow on 11-12 March (L52), which adds an exact date beyond the prompt’s year and answer label.

literalGroups.literal: Великий Новгород — древний русский город на реке Волхов.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The Novgorod State United Museum describes Great Novgorod as an ancient city associated with medieval Rus (L217), and places its historic Trade Side across the bridge over the Volkhov (L220).
Article 1 of the official Ukrainian law states that Kyiv is the capital of Ukraine and its political-administrative center (President of Ukraine portal L230-L235).

literalGroups.literal: Нижний Новгород — административный центр Нижегородской области. Он расположен при слиянии Волги и Оки.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The Russian Emergency Ministry’s regional overview identifies Nizhny Novgorod as Nizhny Novgorod Oblast’s administrative center and locates it at the confluence of the Volga and Oka (L205-L206).

absoluteDifficulty.audienceGround: For an adult familiar with basic Russian history, the 1918 return of the capital from Petrograd to Moscow is a familiar thematic episode but still requires recalling a specific predecessor city. The item is a single-step historical recall rather than broad world knowledge or a multistep inference; MEDIUM fits the thematic-familiarity band. All four alternatives are city names, with historic and administrative associations that make them comparable choices.
absoluteDifficulty.judgment: This is an author judgment for a general adult audience with basic familiarity with Russian history; it does not claim every adult knows the episode. The difficulty remains frozen at MEDIUM.
